edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: Kefir plausibly improves irritable bowel syndrome through a factor-specific pathway documented in the literature, even if the exact size of benefit varies by population and dose.
edges.summary: The strongest piece here is the 2009 Pilipenko rct in Vopr Pitan, which ties kefir to irritable bowel syndrome in a direction that later studies largely support. That makes this edge more about calibrating magnitude and context than arguing over whether the signal exists at all.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
